description_full: Pan Pacific International Holdings Corporation, together with its subsidiaries, operates retail stores in Japan and North America. The company operates discount stores under the Don Quijote, MEGA Don Quijote and MEGA Don Quijote UNY, Nagasakiya, and Olympic names; general supermarkets stores under the Apita, Piago, and Robin Hood names; and retail stores under the Picasso, OSC Amaike, Miuraya, Don Quijote USA, Gelson's Markets, okyo Central and Marukai Markets, Don Don Donki, and Times brand names. It is also involved in leasing space management; tenant leasing; provision of internet services; and development and procurement of products and control of production. In addition, the company provides products under the private brand names, including JONETZ, Robin Hood, EveryDay Real Price, RESTORATION, ACTIVEGEAR, greenstage, cosparade, me&do, Henai Meshi, and eco!on. The company was formerly known as Don Quijote Holdings Co., Ltd. and changed its name to Pan Pacific International Holdings Corporation in February 2019. Pan Pacific International Holdings Corporation was incorporated in 1980 and is headquartered in Tokyo, Japan.

financial_summary: PAN PACIFIC INTL HLDGS CORP is a large-cap consumer defensive business with a $15.2B market cap on $15.4B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +4% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 11% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically, with gross margins sitting at 32%.

The business throws off $613M in free cash flow — roughly 4 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.46× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.8× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage of 27× is fortress-like.
Shareholder yield is only 1.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 34% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
